title: Thresholded elasticity limiter and sampled utilization reporting
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduce a thresholded elasticity limiter to prevent oscillatory scale-ups during short-lived surges.
Add sampled utilization telemetry to reduce cardinality while preserving percentile signals for autoscaler tuning.
New config knobs: window_ms, threshold_margin, sample_fraction, min_sample_size.
Behavioral change: default sampler fraction is conservative; teams can opt-in to higher fidelity for dedicated pools.
description:
Background: We've seen repeated scale-churn in Dedicated fleets when short spikes cause the autoscaler to open capacity aggressively and then quickly scale down, which degrades tail latency and burns commitments. This PR implements a thresholded elasticity limiter that gates scale actions with a temporal margin and a sampled utilization stream so the autoscaler can make decisions from a low-cardinality but statistically representative signal.

Motivation: reduce oscillation and cost while preserving throughput SLAs for tenants.

Design summary: 1) Elasticity limiter: a compact controller (pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter.go) that computes a dynamic headroom threshold based on recent p50/p95 utilization and a configurable margin. Scale-up events are delayed for a short window_ms if the signal is near the threshold; repeated hits escalate to a graceful fast-path. Scale-downs are damped using the same margin but with longer hold-off to avoid premature decommits. 2) Sampled utilization reporting: a lightweight sampling pipeline (pkg/telemetry/sampler.go) subscribes to per-pool utilization heartbeats, performs reservoir sampling per-tenancy window, and emits aggregated percentiles to the controller. Sampling reduces ingest costs in the control plane and avoids full-cardinality telemetry for very large fleets. 3) Configuration and safety: feature flags and per-pool overrides are plumbed (internal/config/autoscaler.yaml) to allow staged rollout and emergency disable. The limiter uses a safe-fallback: if sampled data is missing, the autoscaler falls back to the legacy moving-average estimator.

Checklist:
- [x] Core limiter + unit tests
- [x] Sampling pipeline + integration test harness
- [x] Metrics and dashboards (docs/observability/metrics.md)
- [x] Controlled rollout via feature flag
- [x] Backwards-compatible fallbacks
- [x] Load tests against perf-canary and dedicated-staging (see pipeline results)

Commits summary: * 8d2f3c4 - initial limiter scaffolding and interfaces * f3b9aa1 - implement threshold heuristics and gating * 1b4c2e9 - reservoir sampler and publish path * 5c7d2a0 - wiring: config + feature-flag + e2e test * 2a1f0b7 - docs, dashboards, and runbook updates

Testing and CI: unit tests (pkg/autoscaler/*) cover threshold computation, backoff timers, and fallback semantics. Integration tests (e2e/tests/autoscale_scenarios_test.go) exercise short spike and sustained load scenarios against a local controller; perf-canary runs validated reduced scale churn (median scale events per minute dropped ~45% in synthetic 60s-spike test). CI: lint, unit, integration, and chart validation passed; a flakey e2e test was retried once and succeeded.

Files changed (high level): pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter.go, pkg/autoscaler/elasticity_limiter_test.go, pkg/telemetry/sampler.go, pkg/telemetry/sampler_test.go, internal/config/autoscaler.yaml, internal/api/v1/autoscale.proto, cmd/controller/main.go (feature flag wiring), charts/dedicated/values.yaml, docs/observability/metrics.md, e2e/tests/autoscale_scenarios_test.go, scripts/perf/scale_scenarios.yaml, Makefile updates.

Rollout plan: staged canary on two small dedicated pools (canary-1, canary-2) for 48h with sampler at 10% sample_fraction, then expand to 30% and wider pools after monitoring p95 latency and scale event rate. Backout: flip feature flag to off; sampler publishes a tombstone to signal absence.

Observability: new metrics exported: limiter_decision{pool,tenant,decision}, sampled_util_p50/p95{pool,tenant}, sampler_sample_rate and sampler_dropped_count. Dashboards added and alert tuned to fire on limiter_decision == blocked AND p95_latency_increase > 15% for 10m.

Related work: follow-up ticket ENG-2080 to expose per-tenant recommender for threshold_margin, and SUP-4121 incident references where oscillation caused SLA miss.

Security & compliance: no new secrets; telemetry uses existing auth path.

Migration notes: config keys default to previous behavior; no required migrations.

Known limitations: reservoir sampling may underrepresent very small tenants; we enforce min_sample_size to mitigate.

Attribution: Priya Natarajan implemented the limiter and sampler; Samir Patel wrote the e2e harness; Marco Alvarez reviewed safety boundaries; Evelyn Cho owned dashboards and alerts.

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Can we avoid adding another timer if the controller already has a backoff queue? Suggest integrating with existing backoff to reduce churn.

Priya Natarajan: We investigated integrating with the backoff queue; the limiter needs a separate short-window gate to compute decisions without mutating the global backoff state. Added an adapter that reads backoff state but keeps limiter timers locally.
Evelyn Cho: Dashboard queries look good; please add an example alert query for on-call runbook. Also confirm SLI thresholds used in perf tests.
Priya Natarajan: Added alert query + runbook snippet to docs/observability/metrics.md and included SLI thresholds used in perf-canary in the PR description.
Samir Patel: e2e test is flaky against macOS CI runner under heavy parallelism. Can we mark it as serial in the harness?
Priya Natarajan: Marked the e2e as Serial; CI run now passes consistently.
notes: Performance observation: 60s synthetic spikes saw a 45% reduction in immediate scale events and a 12% reduction in cost for the test pool over a 24h simulated run.
Follow-on: ENG-2080 for per-tenant adaptive thresholds; consider exposing sample_fraction as part of pool SLA profile.
